name: Saudi Arabia

most.note: Check when you last had a tetanus, diphtheria and polio booster. If it was more than ten years ago and you'll be anywhere medical care is limited, a booster is recommended.

some.note: Spread by daytime-biting mosquitoes, and bite avoidance is the main protection. Ask about the vaccine if you've had dengue before.
Recommended for most people going to Saudi Arabia who haven't had it before. It spreads through food and water, and a good hotel doesn't remove the risk.
Worth considering for longer stays, for anyone who might need medical or dental treatment there, and for work with blood or needles.
Make sure you've had two doses of MMR. Measles is common in Saudi Arabia, and a UK adult who missed a dose can catch it.
Worth considering for longer stays with local people, and required for Hajj and Umrah pilgrims.
Worth considering if you'll be around animals, in rural areas or far from medical care, and for children, who are bitten more often. The course takes three or four weeks, so book early.
Spread through food and water. Recommended for most trips to Saudi Arabia, and especially if you're staying with family or eating away from the tourist trail.

certificates: A yellow fever certificate is asked for from travellers aged 9 months and over arriving from a country with yellow fever risk, or after more than 12 hours in transit through one. Flying straight from the UK, you won't need one.

malaria.line: There's a low malaria risk in parts of Saudi Arabia. Bite avoidance is the usual advice rather than tablets.
